title: The Orchard of Bellbird Bay
premise: Jonah Thornbury, a wedding planner who fled her hometown fifteen years ago after a scandal she didn't cause, returns to Bellbird Bay for her grandmother's funeral and the reading of a will that leaves her the family orchard — on the condition she stays through one full harvest season. To survive the reunion of relatives who remember her as the girl who ruined everything, she persuades Eli Marchetti, the orchard's quiet forester and her brother's old friend, to pose as her partner. The fake romance turns real by midsummer, but when the truth of the old scandal surfaces and Jonah's inheritance is contested, she must choose between fleeing again and staying to claim both the orchard and Eli. She stays, testifies to what really happened, and the final chapter is their wedding — planned by her, in the orchard, at last believing in one.
about_author: August Joubert is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade orchestrating other people's happiest days before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn romances set in coastal towns where the past is never more than one tide away.

chapters.title: Return Freight
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fifteen years after leaving, Jonah steps off the train at Bellbird Bay for her grandmother's funeral, clutching a funeral wreath she built herself. The town recognizes her instantly — and not kindly. Beat: dread wrapped in grief, the past arriving before she does.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The will leaves the Thornbury orchard to Jonah, contingent on her staying one full harvest season; her cousin Vivienne, who managed the farm for years, is left a cash settlement and a grudge. Beat: shock curdling into resentment as Jonah realizes the gift is also a trap.

chapters.title: Invitation, Regretfully Declined
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Aunt Rosalind announces a family reunion at midsummer, and Jonah's mother begs her to attend — with a respectable partner, for once. Jonah, who plans other people's weddings but avoids her own life, lies and says she's seeing someone. Beat: panic disguised as confidence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fixes Fences
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli Marchetti, the orchard's forester, finds Jonah failing to start a tractor in the rain. He's the brother of the boy her scandal destroyed, though she doesn't know it yet. He offers to help with the harvest. Beat: wary attraction, both hiding something.

chapters.title: A Proposal of Convenience
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cornered by her mother's follow-up questions, Jonah asks Eli to be her fake boyfriend for the reunion. He agrees — too easily, she thinks — naming one condition: she must actually learn the orchard. Beat: a bargain struck, each certain they hold the better hand.

chapters.title: Lessons in Grafting
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli teaches Jonah to graft apple stock, and their hands keep meeting. He watches her charm the orchard workers she was once too ashamed to face. Beat: the fake arrangement's first real warmth, and Eli's guilt tightening.

chapters.title: Reunion, Act One
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The reunion begins; Jonah and Eli perform convincingly through lunch, and Vivienne watches them like a hawk circling a rabbit. Jonah's old accusers are polite in a way that draws blood. Beat: performance becoming protection becoming something else.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. During dessert, Eli defends Jonah against a cruel toast without being asked — and then, alone on the veranda, they nearly kiss. Jonah pulls back, terrified of wanting things she can't keep. Beat: the fake date stops being fake; Jonah flees to bed.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Eli visits his brother Daniel, who was expelled from school fifteen years ago over the incident that drove Jonah away. Daniel is bitter, adrift, and certain Jonah was to blame. Eli, who has read the old letters, isn't so sure. Beat: loyalty at war with doubt.

chapters.title: The Last Train
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. After a town festival, Jonah misses the last train home and Eli offers his cottage above the packing shed. She stays the night — innocently, then not quite. Beat: surrender, and the morning-after terror of having let someone stay.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Weeks pass; they fall into a rhythm of early mornings and shared suppers. Jonah starts planning a harvest festival to save the orchard's finances, her old skills finally serving her own life. Beat: quiet happiness, deliberately unexamined.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne discovers the will's condition was suggested by the grandmother's lawyer — at Jonah's mother's request — and begins assembling a legal challenge, claiming Jonah abandoned the orchard and the family. Beat: resentment finding a weapon.

chapters.title: Daniel Comes Home
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Daniel returns to town for the harvest festival, forcing Eli to decide whether to tell Jonah who he is. He tells her nothing, and hates himself for it. Beat: the lie calcifying; a first cold note between them.

chapters.title: The Festival
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The harvest festival is a triumph — the town turns out, orders roll in, and Jonah, on the bandstand, kisses Eli in front of everyone. For one night she is visible and unashamed. Beat: peak joy, positioned for the fall.

chapters.title: Old Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Going through her grandmother's desk, Jonah finds letters proving the scandal was orchestrated by a teacher protecting his own reputation — and that her grandmother knew, and stayed silent to keep the family safe. Beat: vindication and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: The Name Marchetti
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah realizes Eli is Daniel's brother — that the man in her bed is the sibling of the boy she was blamed for ruining. She confronts him; he admits he'd known who she was from the start. Beat: the floor giving way beneath the season's happiness.

chapters.title: Winter Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Jonah shuts Eli out and drafts plans to leave when the season ends; Eli, wrecked, finally tells Daniel the truth about the letters, and Daniel refuses to believe him. Vivienne's legal challenge lands. Beat: everything Jonah built begins to unbuild.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the inheritance hearing, Vivienne's lawyer paints Jonah as a deserter. Cornered, Jonah chooses not to flee: she reads her grandmother's letters aloud, exposing the old lie and her own long exile. Beat: the climax — visibility as an act of courage.

chapters.title: What Daniel Buried
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Shaken by the hearing, Daniel finds the teacher, now dying, who confesses everything. Daniel comes to the orchard and, in front of Jonah and Eli, asks her forgiveness — and tells his brother to stop carrying his grudge. Beat: the past released, not erased.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Eli's POV. Winter pruning with Jonah, Eli asks for a real beginning, not forgiveness. Jonah says she needs to know who she is without the orchard, without the scandal, without him — and takes a wedding-planning job in the city to find out. Beat: the hard, honest pause before the resolution.

chapters.title: Blossom
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In spring, Jonah returns — not because the will required it, but because Bellbird Bay is hers. She finds Eli waiting at the station with the last train's lights behind him. She asks him to stay past every last train. Beat: the choice, made freely.

chapters.title: The Orchard of Bellbird Bay
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. One year later, Jonah plans a wedding in the orchard — her own. Vivienne attends; Daniel gives the toast; the trees their grandmother grafted bear fruit. Jonah, who didn't believe in weddings anymore, believes in this one. Beat: full-circle joy, earned.
